strategy.summary: Reproduce skimage PR 7473 by building the buggy commit e5e1742bb411 from source, applying the developer's test diff, and running test_ellipsoid_stats in skimage/draw/tests/test_draw3d.py. On the buggy revision the equal-semi-axis case ellipsoid_stats(10,10,10) raises ZeroDivisionError (or the tightened asserts fail first). On the fixed revision the test passes. Versions are chosen by this plan, not documented: numpy 1.26.4 (reporter's version, Python 3.12 compatible), scipy 1.12 (Python 3.12 needs scipy >= 1.11.2; elliprg is available there).

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scikit-image/scikit-image.git && cd scikit-image && git checkout e5e1742bb411
git apply test_draw3d_pr7473.diff (or patch skimage/draw/tests/test_draw3d.py with the reproducing test diff)
pip install -U pip && pip install numpy==1.26.4 scipy==1.12.0 pytest cython meson-python pythran (build-system requires should be taken from the revision's pyproject.toml)
pip install --no-build-isolation -e . (or pip install -e . if build isolation is preferred), run from repo root so the compiled extensions are built
pinned_because: numpy==1.26.4: chosen by this plan to match the reporter's environment from issue #7472; not a documented requirement, so it is an era-inferred choice rather than a constraint
scipy==1.12.0: chosen by this plan; needed for elliprg in scipy.special on Python 3.12; no documented constraint given in the evidence
python 3.12.2: taken from the evidence environment

strategy.reproducing_test: skimage/draw/tests/test_draw3d.py::test_ellipsoid_stats with the developer's diff applied: tightened atol=1e-6 asserts for (6,10,16) and (16,6,10), tightened surface assert for (17,27,169), and new block asserting ellipsoid_stats(10,10,10) gives volume 4000*pi/3 and surface 400*pi with atol=1e-6
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision e5e1742bb411 with the test diff applied, test_ellipsoid_stats FAILS, either with AssertionError from the tightened tolerances or with ZeroDivisionError at the ellipsoid_stats(10,10,10) call. On the fixed revision (the PR 7473 fix applied on top), the same test PASSES with no exception and all assert_allclose checks within tolerance.
strategy.numerical_probe: Call ellipsoid_stats(10,10,10) and compare against the analytic sphere values 4000*pi/3 for volume and 400*pi for surface, using the same atol=1e-6 as the test.

input_output_examples.input: a = b = c = 10; ski.draw.ellipsoid_stats(a, b, c)
input_output_examples.expected_output: volume 4000*pi/3 (about 4188.790204786391) and surface 400*pi (about 1256.6370614359172), the analytic sphere values

risks: The ZeroDivisionError message says float division, which only arises with Python float operands. If the test passes Python ints (10,10,10) and the code path keeps them as ints, the error may be a different message or the path may behave differently; the reproduction relies on the test's Python-int call and the revision's coercion, which the evidence does not show.

Only the test file's own assertions are known. Whether the tightened atol=1e-6 assertions for (6,10,16) and (17,27,169) fail on the buggy revision independently of the degenerate case is not established by the evidence; the transition is still expected via the sphere block or those asserts.

assert_allclose also applies default rtol=1e-7, so for surface around 37426 the effective tolerance is about 3.7e-3, not 1e-6; results may still differ across scipy versions, since elliprg precision depends on the scipy build.

The bug was reported with numpy 1.26.4 and scikit-image 0.22.0; the buggy commit is a development revision, so building it needs compiled extensions and build tools whose versions are unpinned by the evidence. Build failures would prevent any transition.
No platform or sanitiser dependence is stated in the evidence; the failure is a Python-level exception, so it is expected on any platform, but this is inferred, not documented.
The near-sphere value (10,10,10+1e-6) quoted in the evidence does not match the analytic sphere volume to 1e-6, so it is not used as an oracle here.

oracle.tolerance: assert_allclose atol=1e-6 with default rtol=1e-7, as written in the developer's test
oracle.reference_source: Wolfram Alpha values cited in the existing test comments, plus analytic sphere formulas 4000*pi/3 and 400*pi
oracle.why: The test compares against closed-form values for the sphere and against Wolfram reference values for non-degenerate ellipsoids; the tolerance is the developer's own.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision ellipsoid_stats(10,10,10) raises ZeroDivisionError because the formula divides by (b**2 - c**2) which is zero when b equals c, or the earlier tightened asserts fail with AssertionError because the buggy values differ beyond atol=1e-6 plus rtol.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the degenerate case returns the sphere volume and surface within atol=1e-6, and the tightened asserts for the non-degenerate ellipsoids also hold, so the whole test passes.
